BLOCK — performance/293, exact head d17dae35a62fd7fbf88a17f230a0603d77fafdc4, base 288d0d07, clean detached ../review-293-d17dae3. Answers 01a1f956-dac8-7891-a295-4334011badbd. First C34 round; holding retained until merge.

P293-001 / HIGH: the new pre-signal safety command can hold bounce indefinitely before its shutdown deadline starts. justfile:746-757 resolves tmux and synchronously runs set-option at line754, before kill -INT at756 and since=$SECONDS at757. A frozen/unresponsive server therefore blocks the bounce before SIGINT; the later 30 s and 5 s loops cannot bound this command. Suppressing its exit status with || true does not bound execution time.

Reviewer pij-sufficient-clam independently reproduced this on an owned private tmux server: exact added block stayed pending more than 2.010 s after SIGSTOP, before any SIGINT marker; resuming that server let set-option finish and only then reached the marker. This is a private changed-path witness, not a live fleet measurement, and was not duplicated by performance. Exact log provenance is retained in the cost receipt.

Required repair: give the pre-signal helper an elapsed deadline and explicit failure/timeout disposition. Preserve the off-before-kill safety invariant; if the safety guard cannot be established, refuse the unsafe transition rather than silently skipping it. Count any new timeout/poll helper work. The reviewer reports PM has assigned this deadline repair to the coder for round two; no new-head clearance is implied here.

Remaining cost findings/qualifications:
1. No extra connection task: serve.rs still spawns one task per accepted connection. The select is inside that existing task. New memory is one watch channel per listener and one receiver clone plus fixed notification/select state per open connection, O(C), not one new task/channel per request or HTTP2 stream.
2. Not literally zero steady-state work: the existing connection driver now polls an additional pending changed/select branch. Its overhead follows connection polls caused by request/stream I/O, not a separate periodic cadence. Tokio1.53.1 changed uses cooperative/notification state, and sender closure fans out to remaining connection waiters once per listener, O(C). No CPU nanosecond or fleet overhead benchmark is claimed.
3. The new drain timer is shutdown-only: one 5 s timeout per served listener. Local and remote listeners run concurrently. No new recurring daemon timer, sweep or poll loop.
4. release_control uses the same single spawn_blocking per daemon stop, moved before joins. F238 leave/reap costs remain. Remaining worker/request logical tmux reads after release use the existing fork path, up to one fallback child per eligible logical read: O(R remaining reads) shutdown work, not launch-free merely because sites are unchanged.
5. Budget is not an unconditional ten-second daemon stop: HTTP has ≤5 s in parallel with inherited worker/governance/control joins, preceded by the aborted park-notice join; admitted delivery/publication work and both store pools then share one further ≤5 s deadline. Existing unbounded worker joins/outer control state lock are unchanged. The five-second HTTP bound plus five-second store bound must not be promoted into a deadline for all those other joins.

Bounce/inventory: (c) makes one resolved-path tmux invocation attempt when an old daemon exists and lookup succeeds; current command-v canary is /opt/homebrew/bin/tmux. Shell lookup/command-substitution work is real too. Existing /bin/sleep0.2 drain polls remain nominally ≤5 child launches/s per draining bounce, over the 30 s grace and possible 5 s postkill phase. Nothing per daemon tick/seat. crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs and the control-client/adapter implementation are unchanged in base..head; no new daemon child launch site. Shell helper work is not covered by daemon spawn counters. Binary/socket equivalence and client EOF/retry behavior remain independently reviewer/security-owned, not performance-cleared.

Evidence: artifact://314 exact seven-file diff; /tmp/performance-293-static-cost.json; serve.rs:38-88, lib.rs:349-424, justfile:737-768; locked Tokio watch implementation inspected. No performance-seat code edits, builds, tests, stress reruns, deployment or signals. Focused serve/daemon-stop/released-adapter/clippy executions are reviewer-owned and still separately receipted. Existing user-reported open-stream failure and F238 transition note139074f are retained history, not rerun or relabeled as this head's runtime proof.

After merge: prime owns two bounces; performance has requested signal / old-gone / new-ready timestamps separated from builds and will correlate PID/start/commit. First transition may require SIGKILL on the old binary; second must stop the new binary on SIGINT without SIGKILL. Those deployed proofs remain blocked until merge and are not acceptance evidence for this static verdict.

magicWand: every new pre-signal safety operation needs its own timed failure receipt; a later shutdown timer cannot prove an earlier blocking call is bounded.
